page: Microsoft Azure D64as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 series, powered by AMD EPYC 7763 processors under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, running at a clock frequency of 3.525 GHz. It includes 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Local storage is provisioned with a 550 GB solid-state drive, though no discrete GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded compute and cryptographic performance, driven by hardware support for AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instructions. The instance scored within the top 25 percent in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and PassMark CPU encryption benchmarks, alongside competitive Geekbench multi-core throughput. Cached memory bandwidth delivers high transfer rates, though uncached large-block reads and writes align closer to platform averages. Additionally, the processor lacks AVX-512 extensions, which limits throughput on vectorized float routines specifically optimized for 512-bit registers.

The 64-core density combined with 256 GB of RAM delivers high compute capacity within a standard resource footprint, making it cost-efficient for heavy parallel processing without the premium associated with specialized memory-heavy nodes. Microsoft Azure D64as_v4 is well suited for enterprise web serving tiers, relational and caching databases, large-scale continuous integration compilation, and multi-threaded data transformation pipelines.
